tool.name: Exome CNV calls
tool.description: deletions, duplications and chromosome dosage from target read depth against a same-kit panel
tool.command: #if $reference: ln -s '$reference' reference.fa && samtools faidx reference.fa && #end if python3 '$__tool_directory__/wes_cnv.py' --sample '$sample' --sample-name '$sample.element_identifier' #set $all_panel = list($panel) + (list($extra_panel) if $extra_panel else []) --panel #for $p in $all_panel: '$p' #end for --panel-names #for $p in $all_panel: '$p.element_identifier' #end for #if $reference: --reference reference.fa #end if #if $genes: --genes '$genes' #end if #if $segdups: --segdups '$segdups' #end if --min-depth $advanced.min_depth --p-cnv $advanced.p_cnv --min-bf $advanced.min_bf --pcs $advanced.pcs --calls '$calls' --targets '$targets' --summary '$summary'

param.name: sample
param.label: Per-target mean depth of the sample (mosdepth regions BED)
param.help: The *regions* output of mosdepth over the capture targets (chrom, start, end, [name,] mean depth); in the FASTQ workflow, the per-target coverage step.

param.name: panel
param.label: Panel: per-target mean depth of other samples
param.help: The same mosdepth output of at least 3 other samples of the same capture kit, sequencer and pipeline (unrelated, if possible). A collection of all samples of a run works: the sample itself is dropped by its name. More samples and samples from the same batch give better calls; with fewer than 3 the result is empty and says why.

param.name: extra_panel
param.label: Additional panel samples
param.help: Per-target depth of earlier samples of the same kit (e.g. a stored reference collection), added to the panel above.

param.name: reference
param.label: Reference genome (FASTA)
param.help: GC content of each target, for the GC correction (recommended).

param.name: genes
param.label: Coding exons (BED, gene symbol in column 4)
param.help: The coding-region BED of the workflows: the genes and exons each CNV covers.

param.name: segdups
param.label: Segmental duplications (BED)
param.help: E.g. GIAB GRCh38_segdups.bed.gz: calls with most targets inside are marked low confidence.

param.name: min_depth
param.label: Minimum panel depth of a target

param.name: p_cnv
param.label: Probability that a CNV starts at a target
param.help: Higher finds more small CNVs and more false ones.

param.name: min_bf
param.label: Minimum log10 Bayes factor of a reported call

param.name: pcs
param.label: Principal components of the panel removed (batch effects)

tool.help:
**What it does**
Calls deletions and duplications of one or more exons from the read depth of the capture targets, by comparing the sample with a panel of samples of the same kit (read-depth CNV calling, as in ExomeDepth, XHMM or CoNIFER):
1. Each sample's target depths are divided by its median autosomal depth and corrected for GC content (1 % bins, from the reference) and target length; X is brought to a two-copy scale by each sample's X copy number, so female and male panel samples serve both sexes. 2. The panel's main axis of variation (library or sequencing batch) is projected out of every sample. 3. Each target's ratio to the panel median has an error from read sampling plus the panel's spread there (shrunk towards the typical spread), calibrated per sample. 4. A hidden Markov model (copy number 0-4; 0-2 on a male X; Student-t emissions, so single outlying targets carry little weight) gives the calls, each with a log10 Bayes factor against the normal copy number.
**Outputs**
*Calls*: one row per CNV: position, DEL/DUP, copy number, targets, mean ratio, log10 Bayes factor, the fraction of targets in segmental duplications, panel samples showing the same change (common CNVs or systematic artefacts), confidence, and the genes as GENE:k/n (k of the gene's n coding exons). **high** confidence: >= 3 targets, mostly outside segmental duplications, not seen in the panel, log10 BF >= 5.
*Per-target ratios*: for plots, and as the parents' input of the clinical report (their read depth at the proband's CNVs).
*Summary* (JSON): panel, noise, chromosome dosage per chromosome (trisomy, monosomy, mosaic gain/loss) and the sex-chromosome complement (XX, XY, XXY, X, XXX, XYY; chrY from the 75th percentile of its targets' depth).
**Performance** (GIAB exomes, IDT, NovaSeq 6000, 50x median target depth, 6-sample panel): heterozygous deletions of 5 targets were found in 83 % of simulations, 10 targets in all, 3 targets in 28 %, single targets almost never; homozygous deletions of 2 targets in 75 %; duplications of 5 targets in 74 %. Against the HG002 GIAB v5.0q structural-variant benchmark, all 3 high-confidence deletions were true, and in three GIAB trios all 12 high-confidence CNVs were inherited or unclear in a parent (none called de novo). Deeper sequencing and larger, batch-matched panels find smaller CNVs.
Calls are for research and decision support; confirm by MLPA, qPCR or chromosomal microarray.
